newsitem.title: USA: Ashland explains Q3 loss, sees improved Q4 sales.
newsitem.headline: Ashland explains Q3 loss, sees improved Q4 sales.

text.p: Ashland Coal Inc on Monday said that its third quarter 1996 earnings suffered from the adverse effects of the expiration of contracts with Cincinnati Gas & Electric Company at the end of 1995.
Earlier, the company reported third quarter earnings of $2.5 million, or $.13 per share on a fully diluted basis, versus net income of $9.2 million, or $.48 per share in the third quarter of 1995.
"As expected, the results for the quarter were very weak," William C. Payne, Ashland chairman, president and chief executive said in a statement.
"However, we continue to believe that fourth quarter sales volumes and costs will significantly improve over this year's third quarter," he added.

"The large dragline formerly operated at the Hobet 07 complex began operations at the Dal-Tex complex in August, and its operation for the entire fourth quarter will contribute to these improvements. The quarter will also be helped by the recent commencement of mining operations on Hobet 21's new permit area across Mud River, where mining conditions are more favorable," Payne said.
Ashland Coal's Revenues for the third quarter were $143.0 million in 1996 and $158.6 million in 1995. Coal sales were 5.5 million tons in both quarters.
